title.narrative: Number of relevant transboundary institutions strengthened to improve regional cooperation

description.narrative: This indicator reports on improvements in the institutional capacity of transboundary institutions that result from CIWAs interventions. It is based on the assumption that strong transboundary institutions with a water resources mandate are an integral part of the path towards regional cooperation. This indicator reflects CIWAs focus on longterm engagement in priority basins in order to support the relevant institutions and ultimately help foster regional cooperation.In addition, this indicator captures CIWAs interest in working with multiple entry points to promote cooperation and generate results. Multiple entry points are required to ensure that cooperation leads to sustainable growth. As such, CIWA engages with basin organizations as well as with regional economic commissions, national governments, civil society, academia, Africawide organizations and others in order to tailor the engagement to fit the basins needs and demands.

comment.narrative: Last available value refers to 2017.This is a cumulative latest data value. The result has not been independently verified. Sexdisaggregation is not applicable. The project is multicountry addressing countries sharing SubSaharian river basins e.g. Nile Zambezi Niger Okavango Volta Lake Chad.

title.narrative: Number of strategic analyses and knowledge products used to illustrate the evidence base for cooperation, needs, and challenges.

description.narrative: This indicator will capture how the analytical work CIWA supports is helping riparians identify and communicate the practical need for transboundary cooperation to multiplelevels of stakeholders including highlevel decision makers at the national and regional level. Products are likely to cover issues such as political economy, benefits of cooperation and costs of inaction, implications for poverty reduction and shared prosperity, implications for climate resilience, specific illustrative case studies, etc. Efforts will be made for innovative packaging and dissemination of such knowledge products to stimulate discussion and cooperative action.This indicator is based on the assumption that a solid understanding of the benefits of cooperation, based on knowledge and evidence, will engender and strengthen cooperation and that cooperation will help to achieve the desired impact, sustainable climateresilient growth in the region.Results are aggregated for basinspecific knowledge management and strategic analyses supported by CIWA as well as Africawide or multiple basin works that contribute to strengthened regional cooperation.

comment.narrative: The final value represents the sum of recipients of the single largest UNRWA Programme Budget service in 2023 in each field office comprising of individuals accessing health services in Gaza Jordan Lebanon Syria and the West Bank.

title.narrative: Number of basins with improved engagement of civil society, private sector or academia.

description.narrative: This indicator is based on the assumption that improving engagement with civil society increases public accountability, demonstrates best practice for inclusion of environmental and social issues (including safeguards) and provides a mechanism for addressing grievances. Engagement with the private sector aims to improve competitiveness in procurement and increase the potential for investment financing. Engaging with academia seeks to enhance the longterm development of local professional capacity. This indicator will also capture the development of internship/young professional programs in basin organizations to improve outreach and the development of Memorandum of Understanding (MOUs) or other meaningful working arrangements with academia, Civil Society Organizations, research institutes, and other professional entities.

title.narrative: Number of basins with increased water resources management and development information in the public domain.

description.narrative: This indicator will track progress on what has been identified as a critical issue in African transboundary basins availability of meaningful data, tools, and analytical insights in the public domain to stimulate awareness and better inform broadbased decision support for cooperative approaches to realize system benefits and manage risks.Progress towards increasing water resources management and development information in the public domain will be assessed based on the efforts of relevant institutions to display information, promote access to information or increase stakeholder awareness of relevant information in the public domain. The set of indicators to be measured with corresponding baselines and targets will be unique to each project and/or as defined in the CIWA support plan (CSP). The indicator is based on the assumption that increasing information in the public domain enables stakeholders to more effectively engage in water resources management and development decision making.Among the items that will measure availability of publicdomain data is: basin characteristics, monitoring data, mobile applications, data services, newsletters, bulletins, analytical reports, forums and analytical tools (e.g. simple models, scenario visualization tools).

title.narrative: Quantity of US Dollars financing mobilized for cooperative management and development of international water resources projects supported by CIWA (billion)

description.narrative: This indicator aggregates the potential value of planned and actual investments influenced by CIWA.This indicator captures CIWAs impact of enabling growth through investments in cooperative water resources management and development projects.This indicator will aggregate the mobilized financing of all projects which CIWA has influenced during one or more stages of project preparation.The indicator includes all sources of financing for investment projects influenced by CIWA.Values for mobilized funds will be obtained from formal financial plans and project design documentation. In all cases, CIWA will use best available estimates when calculating values for results reporting. Values for potential projects will be taken from the most recent study available (e.g. feasibility studies, prefeasibility studies, identification studies, multisectoral investment opportunity analysis, etc.) including studies conducted in support of possible World Bank projects and studies or estimates developed by other reputable organizations. When estimates are considered to be dated, undervalued, or overvalued (relevant for potential projects), World Bank experts will be consulted and/or typical costs for the region will be used to project actual costs for the project and CIWA will report the adjusted figures.

title.narrative: Quantity of US Dollars financing mobilized for cooperative management and development of international water resources projects supported by CIWA (billion)

description.narrative: This indicator aggregates the potential value of planned and actual investments influenced by CIWA.This indicator captures CIWAs impact of enabling growth through investments in cooperative water resources management and development projects.This indicator will aggregate the mobilized financing of all projects which CIWA has influenced during one or more stages of project preparation.The indicator includes all sources of financing for investment projects influenced by CIWA.Values for mobilized funds will be obtained from formal financial plans and project design documentation. In all cases, CIWA will use best available estimates when calculating values for results reporting. Values for potential projects will be taken from the most recent study available (e.g. feasibility studies, prefeasibility studies, identification studies, multisectoral investment opportunity analysis, etc.) including studies conducted in support of possible World Bank projects and studies or estimates developed by other reputable organizations. When estimates are considered to be dated, undervalued, or overvalued (relevant for potential projects), World Bank experts will be consulted and/or typical costs for the region will be used to project actual costs for the project and CIWA will report the adjusted figures.

description.narrative: The overall impact of CIWA is to strengthen sustainable climateresilient growth in SubSaharan Africa. CIWA seeks to support riparian governments to unlock the potential for sustainable and climate resilient growth by addressing the constraints to cooperative management and development of international waters. CIWAs focus on waterrelated growth reflects the desire of riparian governments engaged in cooperative management to accelerate development in support of economic growth and poverty reduction. It also leverages the comparative advantage of the programs host institution, the World Bank, to bring knowledge and experience of infrastructure investment across the waterrelated sectors in Africa.

title.narrative: Number of relevant transboundary institutions using improved analytical tools, knowledge products, data, forecasting, and/or capacity for improved water and climate risk management or investment operation coordination.

description.narrative: This indicator reports on improvements in the institutional capacity of transboundary institutions that result from CIWAs interventions. It is based on the assumption that strong transboundary institutions with a water resources mandate are an integral part of the path towards regional cooperation. This indicator reflects CIWAs focus on longterm engagement in priority basins in order to support the relevant institutions and ultimately help foster regional cooperation.In addition, this indicator captures CIWAs interest in working with multiple entry points to promote cooperation and generate results. Multiple entry points are required to ensure that cooperation leads to sustainable growth. As such, CIWA engages with basin organizations as well as with regional economic commissions, national governments, civil society, academia, Africawide organizations and others in order to tailor the engagement to fit the basins needs and demands.

title.narrative: Water Resources Development Strengthened

description.narrative: This result aims to quantify how CIWA supports waterrelated investments with regional benefits that contribute to climate resilient growth.

title.narrative: Number of investment opportunities with regional benefits that have been advanced through CIWA support

description.narrative: Regional benefits are often at the heart of what countries seek from transboundary cooperation. There are investments that require regional cooperation to materialize in a regionallyacceptable manner, as well as investments that are then enabled by cooperation or regionallyagreed investments. The cooperation relating to these investments in a transboundary context could range from notification and meaningful information sharing to generating consensus required for implementation by a country al to joint investments across countries (e.g. the case of the Senegal Basin). The outcome depends on the level of cooperation, regional drivers for cooperation and the maturity and strength of basin institutions. Often, budgetary support for regional projects or cooperative action is limited, therefore useful support which advances water resources development at the regional level could be to facilitate preparation, financing, implementation, and operations of key transformative investments.The indicator is based on the assumption that advancing investments with regional benefits increases growth, shared prosperity and builds climate resilience.Investments are likely to include, but are not limited to, waterrelated investments that improve resilience to climate related shocks, reduce poverty, enhance food security, generate electricity and enable countries to follow a lower carbon growth path. Examples include, but are not limited to water storage and regulation, irrigation, water and watershed management, institution building, hydrometeorological data collection, information systems, hydroelectric schemes, natural infrastructure and maintaining environmental flows.

title.narrative: Number of investment opportunities with regional benefits that have been advanced through CIWA support

description.narrative: Regional benefits are often at the heart of what countries seek from transboundary cooperation. There are investments that require regional cooperation to materialize in a regionallyacceptable manner, as well as investments that are then enabled by cooperation or regionallyagreed investments. The cooperation relating to these investments in a transboundary context could range from notification and meaningful information sharing to generating consensus required for implementation by a country al to joint investments across countries (e.g. the case of the Senegal Basin). The outcome depends on the level of cooperation, regional drivers for cooperation and the maturity and strength of basin institutions. Often, budgetary support for regional projects or cooperative action is limited, therefore useful support which advances water resources development at the regional level could be to facilitate preparation, financing, implementation, and operations of key transformative investments.The indicator is based on the assumption that advancing investments with regional benefits increases growth, shared prosperity and builds climate resilience.Investments are likely to include, but are not limited to, waterrelated investments that improve resilience to climate related shocks, reduce poverty, enhance food security, generate electricity and enable countries to follow a lower carbon growth path. Examples include, but are not limited to water storage and regulation, irrigation, water and watershed management, institution building, hydrometeorological data collection, information systems, hydroelectric schemes, natural infrastructure and maintaining environmental flows.

title.narrative: Number of transboundary institutions with an improved approach to sustainable investment planning and bankable investment preparation

description.narrative: The indicator is based on the assumption that if a basin institution has improved analytic tools, knowledge products, data, forecasting, and/or capacity it will be better able to assess and monitor water resource management status, challenges and opportunities and inform key basin officials and decisionmakers and to better coordinate investment operation. This in turn will enable stronger, and potentially more coordinated, management of water resources and will minimize risk from climate variability.For priority basins, progress will be assessed based on parameters unique to each basin or region as defined in the CIWA support plan (CSP) or project documentation. Improved analytic tools, knowledge products, data, forecasting, and/or capacity could include, but are not limited to, enhancing the quality of decision support systems, extent of monitoring systems (hydrometeorological) and data, modelling tools, case study analysis, quality of disaster risk management systems, quality and timely implementation of the basin management plans, monitoring of the state of the basin and quality of policy at national level relating to international waters.

title.narrative: Number of relevant transboundary institutions using improved analytical tools, knowledge products, data, forecasting, and/or capacity for improved water and climate risk management or investment operation coordination.

description.narrative: This indicator reports on improvements in the institutional capacity of transboundary institutions that result from CIWAs interventions. It is based on the assumption that strong transboundary institutions with a water resources mandate are an integral part of the path towards regional cooperation. This indicator reflects CIWAs focus on longterm engagement in priority basins in order to support the relevant institutions and ultimately help foster regional cooperation.In addition, this indicator captures CIWAs interest in working with multiple entry points to promote cooperation and generate results. Multiple entry points are required to ensure that cooperation leads to sustainable growth. As such, CIWA engages with basin organizations as well as with regional economic commissions, national governments, civil society, academia, Africawide organizations and others in order to tailor the engagement to fit the basins needs and demands.
